subject.title: Agent declared tools != effective session tools: no strict inheritance mode, no visibility, no clipping reason trace

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off strict tool inheritance mode, or should it keep runtime clipping authoritative and only expose better effective-tool diagnostics?
rationale: The requested behavior changes the security boundary between declared agent config and runtime/session restrictions, and it would add config/API surface in an area where repository policy requires explicit product and security direction.

options.title: Diagnostics first, strict mode later
options.body: Expose declared/effective/removed tools and structured removal reasons while keeping runtime clipping authoritative until maintainers approve a strict fail-closed contract.

options.title: Default-off strict inheritance
options.body: Add a config-gated strict mode that fails a session when declared and effective tools diverge, with explicit override-layer reporting and upgrade tests.

options.title: Document existing clipping only
options.body: Keep current runtime behavior and close the feature direction after documenting that declared agent tools are never authoritative over session/runtime restrictions.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics first, strict mode later
recommendation.body: Expose declared/effective/removed tools and structured removal reasons while keeping runtime clipping authoritative until maintainers approve a strict fail-closed contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The current blame/history points to recent ownership of the relevant gateway/tool-policy surfaces, and the decision crosses core security/config boundaries.
